question: Can a scheduler-free accounting signal based on the remaining current-token Decode work already in flight explain the high-load first-token delay?
source: same 34 cached A100 slow-placement physical points used by HIGH_LOAD_TTFT_DIAG_v1

signal_definition.observation_time: the J0 post-event state where the target request transitions from Prefill to Decode
signal_definition.per_competing_decode_request: remaining fraction to that request's next integer Decode-token boundary multiplied by its current profiled end-to-end Decode time
signal_definition.aggregate: sum over all already-active Decode requests except the target
signal_definition.integer_boundary_rule: an exactly integral progress value contributes one full next-token service quantum

comparison_signals: sum of full current profiled Decode service quanta of competing requests
sum of remaining-to-next-token profiled Decode work of competing requests
outcome: reference first-Decode runtime minus J0/J1 predicted first-Decode profile duration
decision_boundary: Mechanism probe only. Do not adopt a guard from correlation alone. If a signal is promising, freeze its accounting formula before classification back-check and held-out validation.
